title: AI video generators compared: Higgsfield, Runway, Kling, Veo
h1: AI video generators: what creators actually use
description: Higgsfield vs Runway vs Kling vs Veo vs Seedance, checked Oct 22 2026: prices, clip length, audio, control, and what saved creator posts used each one for.
answer: As of 22 October 2026, Higgsfield is the one creators in our corpus use most, because it bundles Kling, Seedance, Veo and others behind one plan and plugs into Claude through MCP. If you want one model directly, Kling 4.0 and Seedance 2.5 make the longest single clips at 30 seconds, Runway Gen-4.5 has the simplest API price at $0.12 a second, and Google's Gemini Omni is the cheapest way in at $4.99 a month [[s:g-subs]].
scope_note: prices and specs from vendor pages; usage from our corpus of saved posts, not a same-prompt test

list: **Sora is gone.** OpenAI closed the Sora app on 26 April 2026 and shut the Sora 2 API on 24 September 2026, with no replacement [[s:sora-end]] [[s:sora-dep]]. Some platforms still show old Sora pages [[s:hf-home]].

**Gemini Omni replaced Veo in Google's consumer apps.** Omni 1.1 Flash shipped on 27 August 2026 [[s:g-omni]]. The Veo 3.1 previews on the Gemini API shut down on 22 October 2026, and Veo 3.1 on Google Cloud retires on or after 17 November 2026 [[s:g-veo-api]].
**Kling 4.0 launched on 15 October 2026** with 30-second single clips. Its API is not live yet [[s:kl-launch]] [[s:kl-api]].

sections.h2: What creators used each one for
paras: We read every saved post in the DejaViewed corpus that shows one of these tools in use and grouped them by tool. Posts that only mention a tool in passing are left out. One general tip holds across all of them: seed text-to-video with a starting image for more reliable results ([[e:C-Ad0PoApy1]]).

evidence.label: [[t:higgsfield|Higgsfield]]
evidence.text: The most-covered platform, and the one creators wire to agents. The two S-tier posts drive it from Claude Code: one runs a whole motion-design workflow through the Higgsfield MCP ([[e:DXKFrnQEfEQ]]), the other pairs Claude Code with Seedance 2.0 for marketing video ([[e:DXKani5jWFi]]). Others use it for UGC ads at volume ([[e:DXIpm6TjE5M]]), camera and lens direction in Cinema Studio ([[e:DWBjCwCiVEe]]) and new camera angles from one photo ([[e:c82dcba1352d]]). Four of the ten entries are sponsored Higgsfield posts with income claims we could not check ([[e:DdSYPwEzYEU]], [[e:DcUsVlvpYYu]], [[e:DdKEdJqF3QD]], [[e:DdICMRrt0-H]]), so weigh them lightly.

evidence.label: [[t:runway|Runway]]
evidence.text: Creators value Runway for control and editing more than raw generation. Examples are its node canvas for branching keyframes ([[e:DDIAME6MhzY]]) and video-to-video for driving motion and expression ([[e:C_8ia4lsMB3]]). A hands-on test of public text-to-video needed a few generations to land one prompt ([[e:C9Ai2ERKUHd]]). The corpus has no post on Gen-4.5 yet.

evidence.label: [[t:kling|Kling]]
evidence.text: Fewer posts, and older ones. Motion Brush let creators draw paths for up to five characters in one shot ([[e:DDFdSEDtKZV]]), and a news post marks when Kling opened internationally with free generation ([[e:C91jKVfxtG1]]). Kling 4.0 is newer than anything in the corpus.

evidence.label: [[t:veo|Google Veo / Gemini Omni]]
evidence.text: Google's models show up inside pipelines more than as a destination. Creators automate an eight-part vlog with n8n and Veo 3 ([[e:DLypfhGRhKw]]), and they animate between start and end frames in Flow to build Apple-style scroll animations ([[e:DasLm6opzIO]], [[e:DW7lN7sj2ow]]). The corpus also has the original Veo launch ([[e:C7AUmaYS_tc]]) and the Gemini Omni announcement ([[e:DYiiwmzpRM7]]).

evidence.label: [[t:seedance|Seedance]]
evidence.text: Usually reached through Higgsfield rather than directly. Creators use it for ad and UGC volume ([[e:DXIpm6TjE5M]]) and for hero visuals in AI-built websites ([[e:Dd8Cx9xzUi4]]). One low-tier post uses it to animate an AI persona ([[e:DdXyLUWTJ4Z]]).

rows: It has an MCP server, and both S-tier video posts use it ([[e:DXKFrnQEfEQ]], [[e:DXKani5jWFi]]). Its unlimited generations do not apply through MCP or CLI [[s:hf-pricing]].
Both make 30 seconds in one pass [[s:kl-launch]] [[s:sd-25]].
Image-to-video with fixed start and end
Omni takes a first and last frame, and creators use Flow's frames-to-video for scroll animations ([[e:DasLm6opzIO]]) [[s:g-omni-docs]].
Higgsfield's camera presets and Cinema Studio ([[e:DWBjCwCiVEe]]), or Kling's Motion Control and keyframes [[s:kl-launch]].
Higgsfield's Lipsync Studio and Kling's lip-sync tool; Seedance and Omni generate audio natively [[s:hf-home]] [[s:sd-25]] [[s:g-omni-docs]].
A flat $0.12 a second for Gen-4.5, published per model [[s:rw-api]].
Google AI Plus at $4.99 a month includes Omni in Flow [[s:g-subs]].

sections.go_note: Higgsfield, Runway and Kling links go through our /go/ redirect, which may become an affiliate link. That never changes which tools we include or how we rank them ([our policy](/method#money)). Google and Seedance links go straight to the official site.

paras: Start with [[t:higgsfield|Higgsfield]] if you want to try several models without several subscriptions, or if you drive production from Claude. Pick [[t:kling|Kling]] or [[t:seedance|Seedance]] directly when you need long single shots and will generate enough to justify their own plans. Pick [[t:runway|Runway]] if you edit and iterate more than you generate, or want a plain per-second API. Pick [[t:veo|Google Veo / Gemini Omni]] if you already pay for Google AI or want the cheapest start.
Treat this as creator evidence, not a benchmark. We have not yet run the same prompt through every tool, and most of the posts behind it predate Kling 4.0, Seedance 2.5 and Gemini Omni.

unverified: Whether Runway Gen-4.5 generates audio natively: one Runway page says yes, and the Gen-4.5 help spec does not list it.
Per-second API prices for Gemini Omni and Seedance are derived from published token prices, not quoted per second by the vendor.
Google Cloud lists Veo prices per "count"; we read that as per second.
